units: <cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 8:2">Ḥull. VIII, 2</cite> <he>צוֹרֵר אדם בשר וכ׳</he> one may tie up meat and cheese in one sheet.
<cite ref="Berakhot 23b:17">Ber. 23ᵇ</cite> <he>צורר אדם תפיליו וכ׳</he> a man may tie up his T’fillin with his money &c.; <he>לא יָצוֹר</he> he must not do so.
<cite ref="Tosefta Shevi'it 1:9">Tosef. Shebi. I, 9</cite> <he>צורר</he> he may bandage (a fig-tree when the bark is peeled off).

Cant. R. to I, 7 אני צוֹרְרָהּ לך בכנפיך I (the Lord) will tie this up in thy lap (reverential expression for, my lap), i.e. I shall remember and visit this act upon thee; a. fr.—Part. pass. צָרוּר; f. צְרוּרָה &c.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 14:4">Gen. R. s. 14</cite> (ref. to <he>ויצר</he>, <cite ref="Zechariah 12:1">Zech. XII, 1</cite>) <he>מלמד שנפשו של אדם צ׳ בקרבו וכ׳</he> this teaches that the soul of man is tied up within him (love of life is a natural instinct), or else, when trouble comes upon him, he would detach it and cast it away.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 5:2">Sabb. V, 2</cite> <he>יוצאות צְרוּרוֹת</he> may be let out (on the Sabbath) with their udders tied up.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 22b:8">R. Hash. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>מאתים זוז צְרוּרִין וכ׳</he> two hundred Zuz are tied up in my cloak; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (neut. verb) [to be narrow,] to cause distress; Part. צַר; imperf. יֵצַר (with ל־, or sub. ל־) to be distressed; to worry.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 76">Gen. R. s. 76</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 32:8">Gen. XXXII, 8</cite>) <he>ויירא … וַיֵּצֶר לו וכ׳</he> he was afraid, lest he slay, he was distressed, lest he be slain; Tanḥ. Vayishl. 4.
<cite ref="Yevamot 63b:15">Yeb. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>אל תֵּצַר צרת וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="R00744"><he>צָרָה</he> II</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 3">Pesik. R. s. 3</cite> <he>אע״פ שה׳ הקדים וכ׳</he> although he (Joseph) grieved over it, yet he (Jacob) placed Ephraim before Menasseh.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 3:1">Ib.</cite> <he>היה יוסף מֵיצֵר וכ׳</he> Joseph grieved over it exceedingly.

<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 2:9">R. Hash. II, 9</cite> <he>ומצאו</he> … <he>מיצר</he> R. A. found him grieving; <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 25a:12">ib. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>מי מיצר ר״ע מיצר וכ׳</he> which of them was grieving? was it R. A. or R. Joshua? <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 25a:12">Ib.</cite> <he>הלך … שהוא מיצר</he> R. A. found R. J. in distress.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:6">Cant. R. to VIII, 6</cite> <he>יוצאי … מְצִירִין בהם</he> travellers suffer through them (the rains; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 333">Yalk. Is. 333</cite> <he>מצערים</he>); a. fr.

<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:31">Lam. R. to I, 5</cite> <he>כל מי שבא לְהָצֵר וכ׳</he> whoever is designated to persecute Israel, is first made a chief; <cite ref="Gittin 56b:18">Gitt. 56ᵇ</cite> <he>כל המיצר וכ׳</he>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 104b">Snh. 104ᵇ</cite>. Mekh. B’shall. s. 5 <he>כל המצָרִים</he> (<he>המְצָרִין</he>) <he>להם וכ׳</he> all that are to distress them in the future; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to narrow, close. Y. Taan. III, 66ᵈ (ref. to Job XXXVI, 19) אם סדרתה … מֵיצַר פיך when thou orderest thy prayer, do not narrow thy mouth (be timid in thy demands), but ‘open thy mouth wide, and I shall fill it’ (Ps. LXXXI, 11).
units: <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 927:3">Yalk. Job 927</cite> <he>והֵצַרְתִּיו</he> (not <he>והצרתי</he>) and I closed him up.
<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 2:12">Ruth R. to I, 7</cite> <he>הוּצָרָה עליהם הדרך וכ׳</he> travelling was painful to them, because they walked barefoot.

<cite ref="Shabbat 107b:2">Sabb. 107ᵇ</cite> <he>נ׳ הדם אע״פ וכ׳</he> if (in consequence of a blow) blood is gathered (and congealed), though no bleeding took place; <cite ref="Chullin 46b">Ḥull. 46ᵇ</cite>. Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᶜ top; a. e.—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 46">Gen. R. s. 46</cite> <he>משנ׳ דמו</he> when man’s blood is tied up (runs slowly, in advanced age); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 80">Yalk. ib. 80</cite>.
